To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD38 is a key regulator of astrocyte activation, and that CD38 expression is up‐regulated in human HIV‐1 encepalitis brain.

(1) CD38 is up‐regulated in activated astrocyte cells and HIV‐1 infected brain tissues; (2) IL‐1β is a major regulator of CD38 in human astrocytes; (3) CD38 knockdown reduces astrocyte production of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines; and (4) CD38 may be a novel therapeutic target to treat astrocyte‐mediated neuroinflammation
CD38, which is involved in adhesion, signaling and enzymatic activities, is up‐regulated in HIV‐1‐infected and/or IL‐β stimulated human astrocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of astrocytes in neuroinflammatory disorders.
the role of CD38 as a regulator of astrocyte activation and dysfunction.
the role of astrocytes in neuroinflammation, particularly in HIV‐1‐induced neuroinflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD38 is a novel target in HIV‐1‐associated neuroinflammatory disorders.
CD38 is an important mediator of neuroinflammation.
CD38 is an important factor in the regulation of inflammatory responses and neuroinflammation in astrocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD38 plays an important role in the pathogenesis of HIV-1 encephalopathy, a neurodegenerative disorder caused by HIV infection.
CD38, a key molecule in immune activation, may play a role in neuroinflammatory disorders, such as HIV-1 associated neurological disease, through regulation of astrocytes.
CD38 is upregulated in activated astrocyte and this upregulation is associated with increased proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD38 expression and function are up‐regulated in astrocytes during neuroinflammation.
astrocytes are important players in HIV‐1 brain disease and that they are regulated by a variety of inflammatory stimuli, including IL‐1β, a key mediator of neuroinflammation.
the enzyme CD38 plays a role in astrocyte activation and that it could be a potential target for the treatment of neuroinflammatory disease.
